subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Marine biologist Dr. Abigail Mensah was studying fish that thrive in both shallow and deep ocean waters.
• She examined the swim bladder density, or the amount of gas per unit volume, of the species she planned to study.
• Mensah found that surface-dwelling fish had low-density swim bladders with a density of 0.15 g/cm³.
• She found that deep-water fish had high-density swim bladders with a density of 0.89 g/cm³.
• The density of a fish's swim bladder is directly related to the water pressure at its typical depth.
prompt: The student wants to contrast the swim bladder density of surface-dwelling fish with that of deep-water fish. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: The swim bladder density of surface-dwelling fish and deep-water fish was determined by an analysis of the gas volume in each species.
choices.B: The density of a fish's swim bladder is directly related to the water pressure at its typical depth, as Mensah's research confirmed.
choices.C: Whereas the surface-dwelling fish had swim bladders with a density of just 0.15 g/cm³, the deep-water fish had high-density swim bladders with a density of 0.89 g/cm³.
choices.D: Though the surface-dwelling fish and deep-water fish had different swim bladder densities, Mensah planned to study both types.

explanation: Choice C is the best answer. The sentence uses "whereas" to contrast the swim bladder densities of the two fish types, noting that the density of surface-dwelling fish was just 0.15 g/cm³, far lower than that of deep-water fish (0.89 g/cm³).
